candidato.titulo: A precision T-cell therapy stalls treatment-resistant cancers in clinical trial
candidato.resumo: Experimental drug invika halts progression of refractory tumors by selectively stimulating tumor-fighting T cells.

texto_fonte:
A precision T-cell therapy stalls treatment-resistant cancers in clinical trial
Friday, October 23, 2026
A precision T-cell therapy stalls treatment-resistant cancers in clinical trial
Experimental drug invika halts progression of refractory tumors by selectively stimulating tumor-fighting T cells.
Early results of the first clinical trial to evaluate the drug invikafusp alfa (invika) in humans indicate that the pioneering treatment may be capable of managing cancers that have rebuffed most other interventions, including standard immunotherapy. A study led by researchers at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), Mass General Brigham and Memorial Sloan Kettering found that, at optimal doses, invika was well tolerated and, in patients whose solid tumors had resisted standard immunotherapy, halted disease progression in most and shrank tumors in some.
“Patients whose tumors are advanced — particularly tumors that don’t respond well to immunotherapy — often have their backs against a wall. Few options remain once you reach that point, but these results highlight a more precise means of stimulating anti-tumor immunity that could provide another solution,” said co-corresponding author James Gulley, M.D., Ph.D., clinical director at the Center for Cancer Research (CCR), part of NIH’s National Cancer Institute (NCI).
While immunotherapies have already transformed treatment for several cancers, many patients benefit from them for only a short time, or not at all. Tumors frequently adapt to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapies, such as pembrolizumab, limiting long-term benefits. Other strategies aim to rally T cells, the frontline soldiers of adaptive immunity, but usually do so indiscriminately, commonly leading to severe side effects.
Scientists designed the protein invika to engage a small subset of T cells, two groups of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes specifically. By activating only this narrow population rather than T cells broadly, invika is designed to drive anti-tumor activity while avoiding the severe side effects that less selective approaches can cause. Preclinical studies also conducted at CCR indicate that the drug hits its intended marks and stimulates anti-tumor activity in animal models. This new study describes the next step for invika, detailing the results of phase 1 and initial phase 2 experiments in humans.
The researchers leading the trial recruited patients with a wide variety of cancers, the majority of which had not responded well to ICB. In phase 1, they treated study participants with varying dosages of invika every two weeks to evaluate the drug’s safety and determine the optimal dose. While several participants experienced flu-like side effects, these were expected and generally manageable with additional medication and supportive care. After identifying the lowest dose at which desired effects peaked, the researchers advanced to phase 2, treating participants at this optimal dose.
Of the 27 participants treated with the optimal dose across both phases, disease did not progress in 16 (59.3%) of them. Four (14.8%) participants experienced greater than 30% decreases in the size of targeted tumors, two of whom had metastatic colorectal cancer with tumors of a notoriously treatment-resistant type and were receiving invika as their seventh-line therapy. Another responsive participant had stage 4 non-small cell lung cancer, again with tumors that had repelled multiple therapies including ICB. In participants receiving non-optimal levels, invika did not appear to have significant benefit.
In these patients, the study authors found that the drug fostered growth in the target T-cell populations without affecting any other T cells. They linked the four instances of tumor reduction to the largest shifts in target populations, though, as the authors expected at this early stage, immune activity alone did not always produce a measurable clinical response.
“These results are early, and although signs of immune activity don't always translate into benefit to patients at this stage, it is new and exciting to see activity in patients whose cancers had stopped responding to immunotherapy — a group of people with very few options left,” said co-first author Nicholas Tschernia, M.D., a physician-scientist early investigator in the CCR at NCI. “These findings give us a reason to keep studying this new type of immunotherapy, particularly by combining it with other cancer treatments to continue to seek improved results.”
The treatment sponsor, Marengo Therapeutics, previously announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted a Fast Track designation to invika to accelerate its evaluation as a treatment for antigen-rich, metastatic colorectal cancer. More recently, FDA has granted the same designation to invika for similar solid tumors, regardless of tissue type, following prior therapy including checkpoint inhibitors.
The ongoing clinical trial is still seeking study participants. Patients interested in enrolling in this study may contact NCI’s toll-free number 1-800-4-Cancer (1-800-422-6237) (TTY: 1-800-332-8615) or email [email protected]. More information can also be found at https://www.cancer.gov/research/participate/clinical-trials-search.
About the National Cancer Institute (NCI): NCI leads the National Cancer Program and NIH’s efforts to dramatically reduce the prevalence of cancer and improve the lives of cancer patients and their families, through research into prevention and cancer biology, the development of new interventions, and the training and mentoring of new researchers. NCI’s intramural research program at the Center for Cancer Research (CCR) conducts innovative, transdisciplinary basic, translational, and clinical studies, including research at the NIH Clinical Center — the world’s largest research hospital. Learn more about the intramural research done in NCI’s CCR. For more information about cancer, please visit the NCI website at www.cancer.gov or call NCI’s contact center, the Cancer Information Service, at 1-800-4-CANCER (1-800-422-6237).
About the National Institutes of Health (NIH): NIH, the nation's medical research agency, includes 27 Institutes and Centers and is a component of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. NIH is the primary federal agency conducting and supporting basic, clinical, and translational medical research, and is investigating the causes, treatments, and cures for both common and rare diseases. For more information about NIH and its programs, visit www.nih.gov.
NIH…Turning Discovery Into Health®
Reference
Ryan J. Sullivan, Nicholas P. Tschernia, Claire F. Friedman et al. Bispecific dual T cell agonist invikafusp alfa in solid tumors: the phase 1/2 START-001 trial. Nature Medicine. October 23, 2026. DOI: 10.1038/s41591-026-04711-0

candidato.titulo: Jornalismo da FAPESP está entre os mais admirados do país
candidato.resumo: Sexta edição do Prêmio Einstein +Admirados da Imprensa de Saúde, Ciência e Bem-Estar destaca o trabalho da Agência FAPESP, da revista Pesquisa FAPESP e do diretor de redação Gabriel Alves

texto_fonte:
A Agência FAPESP, a revista Pesquisa FAPESP e o jornalista Gabriel Alves, diretor de redação da publicação, estão entre os vencedores da sexta edição do Prêmio Einstein +Admirados da Imprensa de Saúde, Ciência e Bem-Estar. O resultado foi divulgado na última terça-feira (27/10). A iniciativa é realizada pelo Einstein Hospital Israelita, com organização do Jornalistas&Cia e do Portal dos Jornalistas.
A Agência FAPESP e a revista Pesquisa FAPESP estão entre os três primeiros colocados na categoria “Veículo Especializado em Jornalismo Científico”, ao lado do Jornal da USP. Além disso, pelo sexto ano seguido, a Agência FAPESP figura entre as três mais votadas na categoria “Agência de Notícias”, na qual também concorrem a Agência Fiocruz e a Agência Brasil.
A cerimônia de premiação será no dia 17 de novembro, no Centro de Ensino e Pesquisa Einstein – Campus Cecília e Abram Szajman. Na ocasião, serão anunciados os jornalistas e veículos que conquistaram o primeiro lugar em cada uma das categorias, além dos cinco jornalistas mais admirados do país nessa temática.
A escolha dos vencedores ocorreu em dois turnos. Inicialmente, profissionais de imprensa e de comunicação escolheram livremente até cinco jornalistas para serem finalistas em oito categorias: “TOP 25 +Admirados Jornalistas”, “+Admirado Jornalista por Região” (Centro-Oeste, Norte, Nordeste, Sul e Sudeste), “Colunista” e “Jornalista Especializado em Ciência”.
No caso dos veículos, foram estabelecidas as categorias “Agência de Notícias”, “Áudio” (programa de rádio/podcast), “Programa ou Quadro de TV”, “Jornais e Revistas” (Impresso e/ou Digital), “Site/Portal”, “Veículo Especializado em Saúde e Bem-Estar” e “Veículo Especializado em Jornalismo Científico”.
Os profissionais e veículos com o maior número de indicações nessa primeira etapa participaram do segundo turno da premiação, que elegeu os 25 jornalistas mais admirados do país, além de três profissionais e veículos nas demais categorias.
“A presença constante de jornalistas e veículos de comunicação da FAPESP entre os finalistas dessa premiação é um indicativo fortíssimo de que o compromisso da Fundação com a divulgação da ciência está sendo executado com sucesso”, avalia o gerente de Comunicação da instituição, Herton Escobar. “Não só no sentido de produzir conteúdos de qualidade, mas de fazer com que esses conteúdos cheguem até as pessoas e sejam reconhecidos como uma fonte confiável de informações para a sociedade.”

texto_fonte:
Google lança Gemini 4 Carbon com foco em cibersegurança e tarefas que duram dias
Por Viviane França |
O Google anunciou o Gemini 4 Carbon, seu modelo de inteligência artificial mais avançado até o momento, com foco em cibersegurança e execução de tarefas complexas por vários dias. A ferramenta liderou a versão 5.0 do Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, com 59 pontos, e obteve resultados expressivos em programação, agentes de IA e detecção e correção de vulnerabilidades.
Desenvolvido para lidar com problemas complexos de engenharia de software, o Gemini 4 Carbon executa fluxos de trabalho autônomos por longos períodos. Em testes internos, o modelo trabalhou por dias seguidos para encontrar a causa de falhas sutis em grandes bases de código e sistemas de baixo nível. Durante o processo, também superou obstáculos e aplicou correções nos trechos vulneráveis.
O modelo alcançou 88,2% no SEC-bench Pro, que avalia a identificação de falhas de segurança, 54,8% no ExploitGym, voltado à exploração de vulnerabilidades para avaliar riscos, e 71% no CWE-bench, que testa a correção de código vulnerável.
Segundo o Google, o Carbon dobrou a taxa de sucesso em tarefas de programação segura em relação ao modelo anterior. A equipe do Chrome relatou ainda um desempenho dez vezes superior ao de um modelo de fronteira de outro laboratório na geração de correções de alta qualidade. Já a empresa de cibersegurança Wiz destacou os resultados do modelo em testes de invasão de sistemas web.
Baseado no Gemini 4 Argon, o Carbon também apresenta avanços nos mecanismos de segurança. O modelo não registrou tentativas bem-sucedidas de trapaça no benchmark Terminal-Bench 4.0 e teve taxa de sucesso de 0% contra ataques de injeção indireta de prompts no Gray Swan IPI Benchmark.
O Gemini 4 Carbon chegará ao mercado com os mesmos preços introdutórios do Argon. A cobrança inicial será de US$ 2 por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 10 por milhão de tokens de saída. Os tokens de entrada armazenados em cache terão desconto de 95%. Após o período promocional, os valores vão subir para US$ 4 e US$ 20 por milhão de tokens, respectivamente.
Quando o Gemini 4 Carbon estará disponível?
O Gemini 4 Carbon ainda não está disponível para o público, desenvolvedores ou empresas. O Google adotará uma estratégia de lançamento gradual, com testes de segurança antes de ampliar o acesso ao modelo.
Nesta semana, a ferramenta começará a ser liberada para um grupo restrito de profissionais de cibersegurança. Durante essa etapa, as equipes vão coletar opiniões dos participantes e aprimorar as barreiras de proteção do modelo. A liberação para desenvolvedores, empresas e consumidores nos produtos do Google ocorrerá após a conclusão dos testes e das avaliações de segurança.

texto_fonte:
Logitech lança MX Master 4 para programadores com visual de código e circuito
Por Raphael Giannotti |
A Logitech anunciou o lançamento de uma versão especial de seu mouse topo de linha voltado para produtividade. Batizado de MX Master 4 Developer Edition, o modelo chega como uma homenagem aos desenvolvedores, trazendo um acabamento estético exclusivo inspirado no universo da programação, mantendo o mesmo conjunto de especificações do modelo tradicional lançado no segundo semestre de 2025.
O grande diferencial da edição está na parte visual, que adota um esquema de cores em dois tons de cinza com detalhes em verde vibrante. A estrutura do periférico traz gravações a laser com elementos clássicos de código e referências à cultura dev, como as tags "//" e "</>", linhas que simulam circuitos eletrônicos e a famosa instrução "(Hello, World)". A fabricante também incluiu pequenas referências, como a menção a "0xFF + 1" (referência ao Dia do Programador) e a data 09.17 (homenagem ao lançamento do kernel Linux).
As mesmas especificações de ponta
Embora a carcaça traga um novo visual temático, as especificações técnicas internas permanecem idênticas às da versão padrão do MX Master 4. O mouse conta com o conhecido sensor óptico Darkfield de 8.000 DPI (capaz de rastrear em superfícies de vidro) e a roda de rolagem eletromagnética MagSpeed, que alcança a velocidade de até 1.000 linhas por segundo.
O modelo mantém recursos como o feedback tátil integrado no chassi, o botão Action Ring configurável para atalhos do sistema e a conectividade com múltiplos dispositivos via Bluetooth ou receptor Logi Bolt. A bateria interna de 650 mAh oferece autonomia de até 70 dias com uma única carga através da porta USB-C. O Logitech MX Master 4 Developer Edition já está disponível no mercado internacional com o mesmo preço cobrado pela versão padrão, US$ 120.
Recentemente, a Logitech lançou uma outra versão do MX Master 4 com detalhes em vermelho. E ainda falando em mouse, mas na linha gamer, a marca lançou também o PRO X3 Superstrike.

candidato.titulo: Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 prices hit $2,000, costing more than the RTX 5090 did at launch and with limited stock available — original $999 MSRP long forgotten, with prices now 2-3x higher
candidato.resumo: It costs just as much to buy an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 right now as the launch price for the RTX 5090, with prices now at least two times higher for this high spec GPU.

texto_fonte:
The Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080, Nvidia's second-fastest GPU from its current generation, now costs as much as the RTX 5090 did, on paper, when it launched. Prices have reached $2,000 and higher, with most of the available stock online limited to third-party sellers. If you can find it in stock, it may end up costing you two to three times as much as it did when it launched.
The cheapest, in-stock RTX 5080 available to buy from a reputable seller online for delivery is this PNY RTX 5080 for $1,999 from Best Buy, the same price as the RTX 5090's on-paper MSRP. You might otherwise end up paying $2,299.99, at least, for this Asus ROG Astral mode at Newegg, or you could pay nearly $3000 for this Gigabyte RTX 5080 from MemoryC, now priced at $2,983.23.
Stock for the RTX 5080 is otherwise limited everywhere, with just one or two available for local pickup (in Best Buy's case), and limited options for delivery. You can also find similar in-store-only pricing at Micro Center, depending on location, which has a Gigabyte card for $1,979.99.
You'll also see a lot of the listings online from sketchy, third-party sellers.. For instance, you could pay at least $2,211.17 for this PNY RTX 5080 from a third-party Amazon seller. Empowered PC, the seller for this card, has had 81% positive ratings over the last 12 months, with 202 ratings in total.
Reputable seller or not, this price scale means you're paying significantly more than the $999 launch price for this GPU. As our GPU price tracking shows, though, this isn't an isolated case. RTX 5080 prices have, like the rest of the RTX 50-series, risen steadily since it launched. However, this is the first time that its price floor has been around the RTX 5090's launch price. That PNY RTX 5080, for instance, was being sold for around $1,500 on average back in August.
It's a bitter pill for gamers, though, that the RTX 5080 has now reached and breached the RTX 5090's launch pricing. That GPU has an MSRP of $1,999, although it'll now cost you thousands more. Prices for the RTX 5090 hit as high as $9,500 last month, but the situation is even worse today. What little stock that remains on sale online can be found for as high as $12,000.
The RTX 5080 uses Nvidia's GB203 GPU and comes with 10,752 CUDA cores, along with 16GB of GDDR7 VRAM. Unfortunately, it, like the rest of the consumer gaming GPU market, is being affected by AI. Demand for high-end GPUs hasn't stopped, but Nvidia's attention has shifted to the enterprise market. So, too, has the focus of memory manufacturers, meaning DRAM allocations and production lines that would otherwise produce memory chips for graphics cards have instead gone to feeding the demand for high-margin HBM for AI data centers.

candidato.titulo: Ghostly Cat’s Head Nebula lurks within sight of Hubble and Webb
candidato.resumo: The NASA/ESA Hubble and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescopes recently stared at an eerie star-forming scene within the Carina Nebula, a massive gas and dust cloud located approximately 7500 light-years away from Earth. The two telescopes offer complementary views of the shadowy form, nicknamed the Cat’s Head Nebula, which reflects the 'magical'' process of star formation. Hubble’s visible-light view shows the cat as a dark, elongated dust pillar and hints of young forming stars, while Webb’s infrared-light imagery unveils many stars and other hidden details.

texto_fonte:
The NASA/ESA Hubble and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescopes recently stared at an eerie star-forming scene within the Carina Nebula, a massive gas and dust cloud located approximately 7500 light-years away from Earth. The two telescopes offer complementary views of the shadowy form, nicknamed the Cat’s Head Nebula, which reflects the 'magical'' process of star formation. Hubble’s visible-light view shows the cat as a dark, elongated dust pillar and hints of young forming stars, while Webb’s infrared-light imagery unveils many stars and other hidden details.
Like a spectral form rising out of a cold mist, the Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes have come across a hauntingly dynamic star-forming scene within the vast Carina Nebula, a diffuse star-forming region. The small, select area that was observed by both telescopes is nicknamed the Cat’s Head Nebula because of its resemblance to a cat sitting with its back toward the viewer. The 'head' of the cat is turned to the right, revealing a glowing eye.
The distinctive shape of the Cat’s Head Nebula has likely been sculpted over time by the intense ultraviolet radiation and winds from massive stars in the Carina Nebula. As this stellar feedback erodes the surrounding gas and dust, denser material within the feline-shaped pillar resists erosion, at least for now.
Hubble’s visible-light view shows the nebula as an opaque, dark brown pillar of dust. The cat’s glowing red eye may mark a young star that is still partially embedded in the dust. A ridge of hazy yellow seems to follow the edge of the filament’s right side. This bright rim is consistent with gas illuminated and ionised by ultraviolet radiation from nearby massive stars, potentially driving photoevaporation. This wispy outline is a sign that energetic ultraviolet light from massive, hot stars is impinging on the gas, heating it up and essentially evaporating it.
The diffuse material surrounding the pillar glows blue and cyan above, shifting to yellow, orange, and red toward the bottom. Hubble’s filters capture light emitted by oxygen, hydrogen, and sulfur, along with starlight scattered by dust. These colour variations reveal a complex mix of excited gas, dust, and stellar illumination.
Piercing through dust’s darkness
Webb’s near- and mid-infrared images each offer different pieces of information to help create a more well-rounded understanding of the Cat’s Head Nebula. While the nebula’s overall structure is similar to the visible-light image, the filament becomes more transparent, and its complex surface structure becomes discernable in near-infrared light. On the cat’s left are ghostly wisps of dust and gas, delicate structures exposed to radiation from nearby massive stars.
The bright optical nebulosity visible to Hubble becomes less prominent in Webb’s near-infrared image. Instead, Webb’s near-infrared view reveals a dense scattering of stars that appear blue and yellow in this colour-composite image. Even in infrared light, some stars are still enshrouded in dust to various degrees. The cat’s eye remains conspicuous, while a faint jet-like feature near the cat’s belly could indicate an outflow associated with a young star.The cat’s eye is a more obvious example of an embedded star, while a faint jet protruding from the cat’s belly hints that a young star is located nearby, perhaps within the cat or externally just to its right.
In mid-infrared light, emission from warm dust and carbon-based molecules outlines intricate structures within the nebula. The filament’s bluish and greenish colours highlight emission that includes polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), carbon-based molecules excited by starlight. These variations in colour and brightness may reflect changes in PAH emission, dust continuum, and local irradiation, rather than temperature alone. Delicate globules and strands to the pillar’s left are particularly evident in this mid-infrared view.
To the right of the pillar, a bright light source appears yellow in the mid-infrared image. It lies against reddish emission from surrounding material. A narrow filament appears to cross the source, although the image alone cannot establish whether the two are physically related.
Though the Cat’s Head Nebula is a temporary scene that will eventually disperse, the region is packed with information. Hubble and Webb’s complementary views of the Cat’s Head Nebula are helping astronomers learn more about the elusive, chaotic, and complex process known as star formation.
More information
The Hubble Space Telescope is a project of international cooperation between ESA and NASA.
Webb is the largest, most powerful telescope ever launched into space. Under an international collaboration agreement, ESA provided the telescope’s launch service, using the Ariane 5 launch vehicle. Working with partners, ESA was responsible for the development and qualification of Ariane 5 adaptations for the Webb mission and for the procurement of the launch service by Arianespace. ESA also provided the workhorse spectrograph NIRSpec and 50% of the mid-infrared instrument MIRI, which was designed and built by a consortium of nationally funded European Institutes (The MIRI European Consortium) in partnership with JPL and the University of Arizona.
Webb is an international partnership between NASA, ESA and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA).

texto_fonte:
Insider Brief
- IQM Quantum Computers reports that its cloud-accessible Emerald system has achieved a Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) entangled state across all 54 qubits simultaneously.
- The company measured a fidelity of 0.516 across the full processor with readout error mitigation applied, exceeding the 0.500 threshold cited for distinguishing genuine entanglement from noise.
- IQM attributes the result to improvements in calibration, gate selection and automated state preparation, and says cloud customers can access the system’s full-chip performance.
PRESS RELEASE — IQM Quantum Computers (Nasdaq: IQMX), a global leader in superconducting quantum computers, today announced that its cloud-accessible IQM Emerald system has fully entangled all 54 qubits on the chip simultaneously, a result that shows the system’s computational quality holds up when every qubit is put to work at once. IQM’s cloud customers now have access to that same full-chip performance, so their computations can draw on the entire processor rather than a fraction of it.
These results rank among the strongest reported for any commercially available quantum computer, giving customers access to state-of-the-art, high-quality processors. Until now, a user running a comparable demonstration on IQM Emerald could reliably use on the order of 30 qubits within a single algorithm. Studies on large quantum chips often use only a fraction of the available qubits, commonly 10 to 20, even when the hardware has many more. Emerald’s result shows the alternative: an entire processor working together on one computation.
“Entangling the entire chip means every qubit and every connection between them has to work correctly in the same circuit. Getting there came down to being smarter about how we prepare the state itself, choosing the gate order to keep idle time to a minimum,” said Craig Ciesla, CTO, IQM Quantum Computers. “Our current and prospective cloud customers now have the chance to benefit from the same tools and system performance that made this achievement possible.”
The demonstration used a Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) state, a standard benchmark for large-scale entanglement, prepared across the entire IQM Emerald processor. The result was enabled by a smarter, automated routine for state preparation that selects the best two-qubit gates while weighing gate fidelity against qubit idle time, choosing both the qubits and the gate order to minimize idle time as the state is built. IQM measured a fidelity of 0.515 at 40 qubits without readout error mitigation (REM) and 0.516 at the full 54 qubits with REM applied, both above the classical threshold of 0.500 that separates genuine entanglement from noise.
The result builds on roughly a year of hardware and calibration work across IQM’s technical teams, including an updated calibration methodology, an improved gate set and continued deployment of error-reduction tools such as dynamical decoupling and qubit selection. These improvements led to an error rate reduction of up to 50% for quantum operations in the processor.
The automated state-preparation routine is part of IQM’s broader effort to automate the operation of quantum computers. This development, along with IQM’s AI-driven agentic calibration work, is part of a broader effort to automate the tuning of quantum systems.
Mohib Ur Rehman

- Aomei Backupper Standard: A respectable free backup program if you can tolerate the occasional ad.

- Retrospect 19 Desktop: The pro version of the above covers all the bases, but has a steep learning curve and high price.
- Backup and Restore (Windows 7): Conveniently installed with Windows, and good for imaging but bad for disaster recover.
- MSP360 Managed Backup: Uses a handy web-based console to provide imaging and file backup services for multiple devices at a reasonable price.
- MSP360 Backup: The free incarnation is a worthwhile upgrade to Windows File History.

- MiniTool ShadowMaker Pro 4.6: There’s a lot to like, particularly its unique ability to interface with all computers on a network.
- Macrium Reflect Home: Would likely qualify as our favorite backup software if it wasn’t relatively pricey. It’s an exceptional program that offers everything we want from backup software — full drive/folder backup, ease of use, reliability, etc.
- DriveImage XML: A viable free backup solution, albeit only for MBR disks.
Note that in this article we focus on local-software based solutions, although many also include a cloud component. For cloud-first backup, see our roundup of the best online backup services. Admittedly, the distinction between the two categories is blurring as they each expand their feature sets.
How we test
Our reviewers run each program through the various types of backups and restores it’s capable of — including those requiring boot media. This is largely to gauge reliability and hardware compatibility. We check speed, but such is highly reliant upon the connections and media involved.
If we notice anything is particularly fast or slow, we’ll tell you about it, but creating a functional backup is paramount.
To learn more details, see our article on how PCWorld tests backup software.
Who curated this article
Having started computing by flipping switches, Jon Jacobi has witnessed storage morph from punch cards and tape to solid state. He’s been using and testing HDDs, SATA SSDs, and NVMe SSDs for PCWorld for well over two decades. To paraphrase a well-known commercial, you might say he’s seen a thing or two.
How to choose backup software
If you recently purchased an external HDD or SSD from a major vendor such as Seagate or WD, check to see if there are backup utilities or a backup software license included. Whatever backup software you use, keep in mind the following key aspects of the best solutions: file backup for documents/photos, image backup for whole-PC rollback, boot media for dead-drive recovery, versioning for accidental overwrite protection, and know which are critical to your backup plan.
File backup
If you want to back up your essential data (operating systems and programs can be reinstalled, though it’s mildly time- and effort-consuming), a program that backs up only your important files is essential. Some programs even automatically select the appropriate files or folders. File backup can include operating system files if you wish but is still not suitable for disaster recovery.
Image backup/imaging
Images are byte-for-byte snapshots of your entire hard drive (normally not including empty sectors) or partitions, and can be used to restore the operating system, drivers, programs in one swift, fell swoop. Imaging also ensures that you don’t omit anything important as can happen with file backup.
Recovery boot media
Should your system crash completely, you need alternate means to boot your system and restore data using your backup software. Any backup program worth its salt should be able to create a bootable optical disc or USB thumb drive. Some will also create a restore partition on your hard drive, which can be used if the issue isn’t a failed drive.
Note that we’ve run into multiple issues with Microsoft’s own Recovery Drive and System repair disc — don’t rely on those.
Scheduling
If you’re going to back up effectively, you need to do so on a regular basis. Any backup program you purchase should let you schedule backups and run them in the background. Some even will backup files as they change (real time) or at very short intervals (continuous)
Versioning
Versioning is simply retaining older version of files (or backups) rather than overwriting them during the backup/sync process. You can generally define how many versions to keep, but if you choose to cull older files, this is till not true backup which again, is an immutable copy of your data, drives, or system.
Optical discs
Every backup program supports hard drives, but as obsolete as they may seem, DVDs and Blu-Ray discs are great archive media. If you’re worried about optical media’s reliability, M-Disc claims its discs are reliable for a thousand years, backed up by Department of Defense testing.
Online storage (cloud) support
An offsite copy of your data is a hedge against physical disasters such as theft, flood, fire, and power surges. Online storage services are a great way to meet that need. Some backup software will let you back up to Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, Amazon S3 and compatible, etc. however Cloud Managers can serve as a workaround with backup programs that don’t. The downside to cloud storage is relatively slow performance. Keep a local backup for faster restores.
Network access
Backing up to other computers or NAS boxes on your network or in remote locations (say your parent’s or children’s house) is another way of safeguarding your data via a physically remote copy. If you use network storage, it can also be handy to back them up to you local system.
FTP/SFTP can be used for offsite, while SMB (Windows and most OS’s) and AFP (Apple) are good for other PCs or NAS on your local network. Network support is not universal, and some backup programs allow you to back up to, but not from network shares. Just be careful in the way you expose your computers on the Internet.
Real-time backup
Real-time backup means that files are backed up whenever they change, usually upon creation or save. It’s handy for keeping an immediately available backup of rapidly changing data sets. For less volatile data sets, scheduled backups will do just fine.
Continuous backup
Continuous simply means backing up on a tight schedule, generally every few minutes, rather than in real time, daily, weekly, or monthly. Use continuous backup for rapidly changing data sets where transfer rates are too slow, or computing power too precious for real-time backup.
Performance concerns
Most backups proceed in the background or during dead time, so performance isn’t a huge issue in the consumer space. However, if you’re backing up multiple machines, backing up to multiple destinations, or dealing with very large data sets, speed will be a consideration. That said, backup speed is highly dependent upon the hardware and transport technology in use.
Further reading: Check out PCWorld’s roundup of best external drives for recommendations on reliable storage options — an important component in a comprehensive backup strategy.
FAQ
What is the best Windows backup software?
The best Windows backup software is Easeus Todo Backup 2025. It has everything PCWorld expects to see in a top product: A polished interface, intuitive functionality, a comprehensive approach to backing up data including imaging, file backup, sync, and disaster recovery. And most important, it’s reliable! Todo Backup also offers the option of a perpetual license or a subscription model, the latter of which can be augmented with affordable cloud storage.
What is the best free Windows backup software?
It turns out that PCWorld’s favorite for-pay backup software, Easeus Todo Backup 2025, also offers a surprisingly robust free version. It matches its paid counterpart in basics such as imaging, file backup, sync, and, most especially — disaster recovery. It also features the same eminently user-friendly interface. As with most backup freeware, you will be nagged to upgrade, and Easeus’s optional cloud storage, which is surprisingly affordable, is only available at the subscription tier.
Will backup software slow down my computer?
Backup software typically runs in the background or during dead time, so given even moderately modern hardware, you shouldn’t notice any decrease in performance. Most programs let you throttle the backup process if you do notice a slowdown.
Does Windows Backup and Restore (Windows 7) save everything?
Yes, by default, Backup and Restore (Windows 7) saves everything on your system disk (all the partitions, including hidden ones) in what’s known as an image file that would be suitable for disaster recovery if Windows Recovery Drive and Rescue disk were reliable. News bulletin — they aren’t.
Hence, we only recommend this program for creating highly compatible VHD/VHDX images of your data drives and partitions which can be mounted as virtual drives and browsed using nothing but Windows Explorer.
What’s the difference between Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, etc. and backup software?
Google Drive, Dropbox, and OneDrive are what’s known as cloud storage, or online storage. They create a local virtual drive that you can drag files to, and which is eventually synced to the cloud as time allows. They also provide a Web portal where you can manage your files remotely.
However, by default these services sync changes in the data across all devices. True backups should be immutable snapshots that may be added to but not changed. Some services offer versioning (keeping older files, and adding new ones), which creates a close approximation to backup.
Cloud backup services (distinct from those mentioned above) offer many, though not all, of the benefits of Windows backup software. This is generally done with local client software that offers just basic functions like file backup and sync. You can learn more about these in our roundup of best cloud backup services.
How often should backups be scheduled?
Ideally, as often as your data changes. If you are working on an important project or have work that you absolutely cannot afford to lose, you should consider real time (as data changes) or continuous (very short intervals). Hourly, daily, or longer intervals will be fine for the average user. All file backups should be augmented by weekly or monthly system backups.
Can I back up files to and from my cloud storage?
Until a few years ago, most Windows backup software was restricted to making local backups — i.e., to another drive, external or internal, connected to your system. There were of course services such as Mozy that had their own backup clients, but that’s covered in our online backup roundup. Here we’re talking just plain backup programs.
The situation is improving rapidly, and many backup software vendors are adding online storage services as destinations for their backups.
If your favorite backup program doesn’t support cloud storage directly, a cloud storage manager that integrates online storage services into File Explorer can make online backup possible with just about any backup app.
What’s the difference between full, differential, and incremental backup?
A full backup is a backup of all your data, regardless of how new or old it is. A differential backup is all the data that’s changed since your last full backup. An incremental backup is all the data that’s changed since any your original full and/or the last differential/incremental backup. Differential and incremental backups require a initial full backup to be restored.
Differential backups require more time to create than incremental backups, but are quicker to restore since you only need the latest iteration. Differential backups can grow to be quite large if you don’t perform full backups very often.
Incremental backups take less time to produce and are smaller, but take longer to restore as all of them created since the last full backup must be restored in the order in which they were created.
What’s the difference between image backup, system backup, and file backup?
An image is low-level backup of all the sectors (including “empty” sectors if you wish) contained by a disk or partition, regardless of their pertinence to your files. It’s basically fool-proof in terms of accidentally overlooking important data.
A system backup is an disk image backup of all the partitions on your system drive. This includes several that are hidden, i.e., not enumerated as drive letters by the operating system. A system backup might also include other drives, but must contain the OS drive.
A file backup is a high-level backup of data read via the operating system’s file system. Most often this is data, but may include all the files on a drive.
What should I back up?
In truth, it’s only your essential personal data that must absolutely, positively, 100% be backed up. Once the family pictures or your work-in-progress are trashed with no backup, there’s no way back other than an expensive recovery service, and even that’s not guaranteed if the physical media is unreadable.
On the other hand, a system backup is exceedingly handy for getting you back up to speed with minimal hassle. It returns your system to exactly where you were at the time of the backup: OS, program, updates, upgrades, settings, data are all back in a relative blink of the eye.
But it’s not essential. While reinstalling operating systems, drivers, and programs, as well as adjusting settings require more effort, you can then recover your data if that’s all you backed up. See the first paragraph.

Com o material disponível, o usuário pode pedir um resumo, consultar um assunto mencionado ou fazer perguntas sobre o conteúdo. Em uma reunião, por exemplo, pode solicitar uma lista das decisões; em uma aula, pedir a explicação dos conceitos apresentados.
O Google também sugere combinar a gravação com fotos de anotações manuscritas. Assim, a explicação oral de um professor pode ser analisada junto de uma fórmula ou de um esquema registrado no caderno. O gravador já havia sido apresentado pela empresa em setembro, em um pacote de recursos para estudo.
Como gravar aulas e reuniões pelo aplicativo
Veja abaixo como gravar usando o app.
2. Toque no microfone. Nos notebooks existentes, ele fica na aba Fontes.
3. Autorize o uso do microfone, se solicitado, e comece a gravar.
4. Use Pausar para interromper e retomar a captura.
5. Toque em Parar para encerrar e consultar a transcrição.
O Google orienta pedir autorização às outras pessoas antes de gravá-las. Também recomenda conferir as respostas da IA, que pode cometer erros ao interpretar os materiais.

candidato.titulo: Bacteria can alter the toxicity and affect the biosafety of nanomaterials
candidato.resumo: Graphene-based materials have been explored for innovative technological applications in electronic devices, high-performance plastics, and biotechnology

texto_fonte:
The most surprising discovery occurred when the researchers combined graphene oxide with silver ions. The analyses showed that the formation of the ecocorona significantly increased the ability of graphene oxide to associate with silver. This result, combined with the greater accumulation of the metal observed in the organisms, helps explain the “Trojan Horse” effect identified in the study.
The effects were observed in different parts of C. elegans. The combination caused intestinal, neuronal, and reproductive alterations. It was also the treatment that caused the most destruction of the nematode’s reproductive cells, even at lower concentrations of silver.
In addition to the effects observed, the study has implications for the process of assessing nanomaterial safety itself. Since E. coli is routinely used as food in C. elegans assays, disregarding its interaction with the tested materials may influence the interpretation of the results. The findings reinforce the importance of considering these interactions in the design and interpretation of nanotoxicity studies, contributing to more robust assessments in the development of protocols, technical standards and regulatory provisions.
The study was conducted by CNPEM in collaboration with USP’s Center for Nuclear Energy in Agriculture, the C. elegans group of the Federal University of Pampa (Unipampa), and the Environmental Nanoscience group of the University of Birmingham, in the United Kingdom, with financial support from the Coordination for the Improvement of Higher Education Personnel (Capes), the National Council for Scientific and Technological Development (CNPq), and the São Paulo Research Foundation (Fapesp).
The article Caenorhabditis elegans in nanosafety research: dual effect of Escherichia coli ecocorona formation on single and combined toxicity of graphene oxide is available online.

texto_fonte:
Após vazamento, Smart Sampa exigirá reconhecimento facial para acessar câmeras
Por Marcelo Fischer |
A Prefeitura de São Paulo anunciou a exigência de reconhecimento facial para os profissionais autorizados a acessar imagens e informações do Smart Sampa. A medida foi apresentada pelo prefeito Ricardo Nunes (MDB) na terça-feira (27), uma semana após a revelação de um vazamento de credenciais do sistema de vigilância.
Segundo Nunes, a autenticação passou a valer naquele dia para agentes da Guarda Civil Metropolitana (GCM) e para os nove promotores que terão acesso à plataforma por meio de uma parceria com o Ministério Público de São Paulo (MPSP). A checagem identifica quem consulta o sistema.
O Smart Sampa reúne câmeras públicas e privadas e usa reconhecimento facial para procurar pessoas em bases de foragidos e desaparecidos. A plataforma também identifica placas de veículos e emite alertas para as equipes de segurança.
O que ficou exposto no vazamento
Em 20 de outubro, o UOL revelou que um repositório público expôs informações restritas por cerca de 11 meses. O material incluía 181 logins e senhas, dados de mais de 6 mil agentes de segurança e instruções para reproduzir uma interface de acesso ao Smart Sampa.
As credenciais permitiam consultar imagens de uma rede com mais de 58 mil câmeras, inclusive em creches, escolas, unidades de saúde e serviços de atendimento a dependentes químicos. Para comprovar o acesso em tempo real, a reportagem acompanhou a própria imagem em oito câmeras de totens privados conveniados, nos Campos Elíseos, no centro da capital.
Nunes nega que tenha ocorrido uma invasão ou falha de segurança da plataforma. A gestão atribui o episódio ao compartilhamento ilegal de dados por um guarda municipal, identificado e afastado. A conduta do servidor é investigada pela Corregedoria da GCM.
Para o Instituto de Defesa de Consumidores (Idec), a responsabilização de um funcionário não dispensa a avaliação dos controles de proteção. A entidade cobra auditoria independente e uma demonstração de como o sistema impede que credenciais expostas deem acesso a imagens e informações sigilosas.
O que está sob apuração
O MPSP registrou uma Notícia de Fato para analisar os indícios apresentados pela reportagem. Esse é um procedimento preliminar: cabe ao promotor responsável decidir se há elementos para instaurar um inquérito civil.
A Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) também foi acionada. Onze organizações da sociedade civil pediram a apuração das responsabilidades da Prefeitura e da Sentinelx, empresa ligada à tecnologia do programa. Segundo o UOL, a agência cobrou esclarecimentos da administração municipal, com prazo de cinco dias.
O pedido das entidades inclui avaliar a notificação das pessoas afetadas, adotar medidas preventivas e exigir um Relatório de Impacto à Proteção de Dados Pessoais. As organizações contestam o argumento da Prefeitura de que o programa estaria dispensado dessa obrigação por se enquadrar na exceção da Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD) para segurança pública.
Entre os pontos questionados estão o monitoramento de crianças e de pacientes e os usos da plataforma além da repressão criminal, como a localização de desaparecidos. As entidades pedem uma avaliação específica da legalidade da vigilância em escolas e serviços de saúde.
Perícia e abordagens equivocadas ampliam as críticas
O programa também é alvo de uma ação civil pública iniciada em 2023 pelo Laboratório de Políticas Públicas e Internet (Lapin), pelo Instituto de Referência Negra Peregum e pela Defensoria Pública de São Paulo. A Justiça manteve a determinação de uma perícia independente em decisão anterior à divulgação do vazamento.
O exame deve avaliar a segurança da informação, o tratamento de dados e a precisão do reconhecimento facial, incluindo possíveis diferenças nas taxas de erro entre grupos da população. O Núcleo de Estudos da Violência da Universidade de São Paulo (NEV-USP) foi indicado para auxiliar no trabalho, condicionado à confirmação de participação e da equipe responsável.
Relatórios municipais analisados pelo UOL registraram 268 conduções a delegacias seguidas de liberação entre novembro de 2024 e maio de 2026. Desse total, 75 envolveram inconsistências no reconhecimento facial, 181 estavam relacionadas a mandados desatualizados e 12 a problemas cadastrais.
A transparência sobre os algoritmos é outra contestação. Segundo o Idec, a Prefeitura informou não ter acesso ao código-fonte, aos modelos de inteligência artificial nem às bases usadas para treiná-los, além de não realizar auditorias independentes desses modelos. A entidade aponta riscos de discriminação, especialmente contra a população negra.
Na Câmara Municipal, a vereadora Amanda Paschoal (PSOL) apresentou, em 20 de outubro, um requerimento para criar uma Comissão Parlamentar de Inquérito (CPI) sobre o programa.
Prefeitura amplia uso do sistema com o Ministério Público
O anúncio da autenticação facial ocorreu durante a assinatura de dois convênios entre a Prefeitura e o MPSP. Um deles prevê o compartilhamento de imagens e informações com o Grupo de Atuação Especial de Repressão ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco), para apoiar investigações. O acordo tem validade inicial de 12 meses.
O outro, com duração de 60 meses, integra o programa Alerta de Proteção Integrada. A proposta é localizar agressores que ainda não tenham sido notificados sobre medidas protetivas e emitir alertas para que a GCM faça a comunicação da decisão judicial.
A identificação usará uma base de informações fornecida pelo Ministério Público. Durante a cerimônia, Nunes também anunciou a expansão da rede com mais 20 mil câmeras; o comunicado municipal informa que o programa já reúne mais de 50 mil equipamentos.
